newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Deutsche pledges further backing for MGAM.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Deutsche pledges further backing for MGAM.

text.p: Investors who have stuck by three stricken Morgan Grenfell investment funds were on Wednesday given the full backing of Morgan Grenfell's owners German banking heavyweight Deutsche Bank AG.

Deutsche's backing pledge came as Britain's investments watchdog investigating irregularities in the funds, temporarily suspended from trading last week, warned the inquiry into what went wrong and whether compensation is due will take some time.
"Judging by past experience, this type of investigation takes months rather than weeks," Judy Delaforce of the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) said.

Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) said that if necessary Deutsche, its ultimate parent, would buy units in the two unit trusts and shares in the investment fund currently under the microscope of forensic accountants.
It will provide this support for a minimum of three months to ensure the smooth running of the funds.

The latest commitment was approved by IMRO, and Delaforce said the watchdog was happy with the present make-up of the funds, which were suspended because of suspected misvaluations of certain unlisted stocks.

"We are satisfied that all stocks with any slight question mark over them have been removed from the portfolio as part of the 180 million pound ($280 million) injection that was made by Deutsche Bank," Delaforce told Reuters.
Earlier, Morgan Grenfell spokesman James Murray said Wednesday's commitment was in addition to cash balances in the funds.

Last week these stood at 300 million pounds, following the 180 million cash injection by Deutsche. But these balances are funding investor redemptions, which late on Tuesday reached 256 million pounds since trading resumed last Thursday morning.

Murray said the rate of redemptions in the MG European Growth Trust, the MG Europa Fund and the Morgan Grenfell International Funds' MG European Capital Growth Fund had slowed significantly, and there was currently sufficient cash in each.

After an initial flight from the funds, the rate of redemptions has slowed, with only 24 million pounds redeemed on Tuesday, compared with 39 million on Monday and a total of 193 million last Thursday and Friday.
After three months, the arrangements, which were also approved by the Central Bank of Ireland because one of the funds was listed in Dublin, can be ended or changed with 14 days notice, MGAM said.

Last week, MGAM halted trading in the three funds, which had totalled 1.4 billion pounds, but resumed it two days later. Deutsche Bank has said throughout that the 90,000 investors would not lose out as a result of any irregularities.

MGAM, aided by accountants Ernst & Young and lawyers Slaughter & May, and IMRO, aided by accountants Deloitte Touche, are now working to establish if compensation is due to investors as a result of any incorrect valuations of shares.

Deutsche, which has been aggressively building its investment banking business through London-based Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, has been thrust unwillingly into the spotlight and even its coveted triple-A credit rating has come under scrutiny.
But disquiet over its British fund management arm did not prevent a Deutsche financing subsidiary from launching a $250 million bond on Wednesday.
A Deutsche Morgan Grenfell official said the bonds were likely to perform well because of strong demand in the sector.
The bonds come with an explicit guarantee from Deutsche Bank and were priced to give the same yield as U.S. treasury bonds.
"Comparable bonds are trading at six or seven basis points below treasuries, so this issue is also likely to tighten," the DMG official told Reuters.
